<td id="S10.T8.5.4.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><math id="S10.T8.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".996\pm.003" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn mathsize="0.900em">.996</mn><mo mathsize="0.900em">±</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">.003</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.996\pm.003</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S10.T8.5.4.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="S10.T8.5.4.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">.993</span></td>
<td id="S10.T8.5.4.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="S10.T8.5.4.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">.993</span></td>
<td id="S10.T8.5.4.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="S10.T8.5.4.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">.993</span></td>
<td id="S10.T8.5.4.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="S10.T8.5.4.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">.993</span></td>
<td id="S10.T8.5.4.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><math id="S10.T8.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.000\pm.000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn mathsize="0.900em">1.000</mn><mo mathsize="0.900em">±</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">.000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.000\pm.000</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S10.T8.5.4.8" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><math id="S10.T8.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[.993,.998]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">[</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">.993</mn><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">.998</mn><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[.993,.998]</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>
<tr id="S10.T8.5.5" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S10.T8.5.5.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb"><span id="S10.T8.5.5.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">RF</span></td>
<td id="S10.T8.5.5.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><math id="S10.T8.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".995\pm.003" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn mathsize="0.900em">.995</mn><mo mathsize="0.900em">±</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">.003</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.995\pm.003</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S10.T8.5.5.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="S10.T8.5.5.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">.993</span></td>
<td id="S10.T8.5.5.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="S10.T8.5.5.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">.993</span></td>
<td id="S10.T8.5.5.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="S10.T8.5.5.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">.993</span></td>
<td id="S10.T8.5.5.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="S10.T8.5.5.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">.993</span></td>
<td id="S10.T8.5.5.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><math id="S10.T8.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.000\pm.000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn mathsize="0.900em">1.000</mn><mo mathsize="0.900em">±</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">.000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.000\pm.000</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S10.T8.5.5.8" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><math id="S10.T8.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[.993,.997]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">[</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">.993</mn><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">.997</mn><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[.993,.997]</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S10.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S10.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ 10. Multi-Seed Evaluation ‣ What Does It Take to Detect an AI Agent? Minimal Feature Sets for Behavioral Detection under Browser Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> shows that agent F1 = 1.000 in all 30 runs: zero misclassifications across 10 seeds <math id="S10.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> 3 model families. Macro-F1 variance is small (<math id="S10.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\leq 0.006" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>0.006</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\leq 0.006</annotation></semantics></math>). For the evasion ladder (GBM, all 41 continuous+binary+indicator features), detection rate is 1.000 <math id="S10.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> 0.000 at all five levels across all seeds: none (1,025/1,025), rule-based (150/150), GAN (300/300), GAN+ (300/300), and human replay (524/524), all <math id="S10.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> 10 seeds. Not a single agent session is misclassified at any evasion level in any run. With <math id="S10.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>154 agent test samples per seed and 0 errors, the Clopper-Pearson 95% confidence interval for the per-seed agent detection rate is <math id="S10.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0.976,1.000]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0.976</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1.000</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0.976,1.000]</annotation></semantics></math>, and the pooled interval across all 10 seeds and all 5 evasion levels (2,299 agent sessions <math id="S10.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> 10 seeds = 22,990 predictions, 0 errors) is <math id="S10.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0.99984,1.000]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0.99984</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1.000</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0.99984,1.000]</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S11" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">11. </span>Results Summary</h2>

<section id="S11.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">11.1. </span>Feature Importance Ranking</h3>

<div id="S11.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S11.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We rank all 16 features by a composite importance score: 1 point for solo-perfect detection at <math id="S11.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> = 1 plus backward elimination rank normalized to <math id="S11.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> (later removal = higher rank). Figure <a href="#S11.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 11.1. Feature Importance Ranking ‣ 11. Results Summary ‣ What Does It Take to Detect an AI Agent? Minimal Feature Sets for Behavioral Detection under Browser Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> shows the ranking.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S11.F5" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2607.26935v1/fig4_feature_importance_ranking.png" id="S11.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/332;" width="476" height="332" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S11.F5.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 5</span>. </span><span id="S11.F5.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Feature importance ranking. The top features combine solo-perfect detection capability with late removal in backward elimination. Features are colored by category: trajectory (blue), click (orange), timing (red), agent-specific (green).</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S11.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S11.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The ranking reveals that event-stream features (<span id="S11.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">mouse_event_rate</span>, <span id="S11.SS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">click_duration_std</span>, and <span id="S11.SS1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">typing_speed_std</span>) are the last to be removed by backward elimination and appear most often in small perfect subsets. Trajectory features (<span id="S11.SS1.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">trajectory_entropy</span>, <span id="S11.SS1.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">movement_efficiency</span>) are removed first with no performance loss. This aligns with the evasion ladder results: trajectory-level evasion (Levels 2–5) is matchable, but event-rate and click-duration structure are not.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S11.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">11.2. </span>Feature Distributions Across Classes</h3>

<div id="S11.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S11.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S11.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 11.2. Feature Distributions Across Classes ‣ 11. Results Summary ‣ What Does It Take to Detect an AI Agent? Minimal Feature Sets for Behavioral Detection under Browser Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> shows why these features work: agents occupy a behaviorally distinct region from both humans and bots. On <span id="S11.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">teleport_click_ratio</span> (redefined as “fraction of clicks preceded within 100 ms by a raw-event mousemove jump”), all 1,025 Playwright-driven agent sessions are at exactly 0 (Playwright emits no such raw jumps at all), while humans cluster around 0.05 and bots spread between 0 and 1. The separation is therefore an <em id="S11.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">empty-value vs. positive-value</em> signature, made explicit to the classifier through the paired <span id="S11.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">has_teleport_click_ratio</span> missingness indicator. The agent distribution is non-overlapping with both other classes through the combination of the feature and its indicator, which is why even a two-feature classifier achieves 100% agent recall.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S11.F6" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2607.26935v1/fig_feature_distributions.png" id="S11.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/125;" width="476" height="125" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S11.F6.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 6</span>. </span><span id="S11.F6.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Feature distributions across the three traffic classes. Agents (blue) occupy a distinct region from humans (green) and bots (red) on the top discriminative features. On <span id="S11.F6.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">teleport_click_ratio</span> (raw-event definition) the agent column is at exactly <math id="S11.F6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> for all 1,025 Playwright sessions (an empty-value signature rather than a distinctive positive value), while bots and humans take positive values. Combined with the <span id="S11.F6.6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">has_</span>-indicator channels this makes the agent class linearly separable from two features.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S11.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">11.3. </span>Key Findings</h3>

<div id="S11.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="S11.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S11.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(1)</span> 
<div id="S11.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S11.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S11.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Detection is easy under API-driven automation because automation APIs do not emit the raw pointer-move and wheel-delta streams that a physical input device produces.</span> The signature is an <em id="S11.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">absence</em> pattern (zero raw-event teleports before clicks, zero scroll deltas, sparse or empty pre-click mousemove tracks) surfaced through explicit missingness indicators. It is stable across 10 seeds and 3 model families (30 runs, zero agent misclassifications; §<a href="#S10" title="10. Multi-Seed Evaluation ‣ What Does It Take to Detect an AI Agent? Minimal Feature Sets for Behavioral Detection under Browser Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S11.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(2)</span> 
<div id="S11.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S11.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S11.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">The detection signal is an API execution artifact, not an agent cognition signal.</span> Backward elimination removes <span id="S11.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">teleport_click_ratio</span> at step 9 and all four original “pause-think-act” features (<span id="S11.I1.i2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">inter_action_gap_variance</span>, <span id="S11.I1.i2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">inter_action_gap_bimodality</span>, <span id="S11.I1.i2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">action_burst_ratio</span>, <span id="S11.I1.i2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">time_to_first_action</span>) by step 10 without breaking agent recall. The surviving 2-feature necessary set {<span id="S11.I1.i2.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">mouse_event_rate</span>, <span id="S11.I1.i2.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">click_duration_std</span>} contains no cognition-correlated feature; the signal lives in how browser automation APIs generate events.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S11.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(3)</span> 
<div id="S11.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S11.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S11.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Two features are sufficient for 100% agent detection with unit agent precision; five features reach macro-F1 <math id="S11.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\geq" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>≥</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq</annotation></semantics></math> 0.99.</span> The <math id="S11.I1.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> = 2 best exhaustive subset {<span id="S11.I1.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">mouse_event_rate</span>, <span id="S11.I1.i3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">teleport_click_ratio</span>} gives held-out test macro-F1 = 0.926 with agent precision = 0.994 and ROC-AUC = 1.000 at every evasion level; the backward-elimination 2-feature set {<span id="S11.I1.i3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">mouse_event_rate</span>, <span id="S11.I1.i3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">click_duration_std</span>} gives macro-F1 = 0.904 with agent precision = 1.000 and the same ROC. Five features lift macro-F1 to 0.991 (Table <a href="#S9.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 9.1. Exhaustive Search ‣ 9. Feature Subset Optimization ‣ What Does It Take to Detect an AI Agent? Minimal Feature Sets for Behavioral Detection under Browser Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>). On the full 17-feature set, 10-seed macro-F1 95% CIs are <math id="S11.I1.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0.986,0.994]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0.986</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.994</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0.986,0.994]</annotation></semantics></math> (SAINT), <math id="S11.I1.i3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0.993,0.997]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0.993</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.997</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0.993,0.997]</annotation></semantics></math> (RF), and <math id="S11.I1.i3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0.993,0.998]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0.993</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.998</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0.993,0.998]</annotation></semantics></math> (GBM) (Table <a href="#S10.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ 10. Multi-Seed Evaluation ‣ What Does It Take to Detect an AI Agent? Minimal Feature Sets for Behavioral Detection under Browser Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S11.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(4)</span> 
<div id="S11.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S11.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S11.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">The <math id="S11.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> = 1 regime is a diagnostic trap, not a deployable result.</span> The one solo-“perfect” feature (<span id="S11.I1.i4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">cursor_path_linearity</span>) achieves 100% agent recall only by collapsing the classifier to always predict “agent” (agent precision = 0.33, macro-F1 = 0.17, ROC-AUC = 0.50). This failure mode is invisible to a recall-only evaluation; our per-level confusion matrices and mixed-set ROC/PR metrics (§<a href="#S9" title="9. Feature Subset Optimization ‣ What Does It Take to Detect an AI Agent? Minimal Feature Sets for Behavioral Detection under Browser Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>) catch it automatically.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S11.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(5)</span> 
<div id="S11.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S11.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S11.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">15/17 features are redundant within our experimental scope.</span> The first 8 features removed by backward elimination <em id="S11.I1.i5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">improve</em> held-out F1 (from 0.987 to 0.996) by reducing overfitting; features that are redundant here may become necessary on harder distributions (e.g. agents operating through alternative frameworks or OS-level input simulation).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S11.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(6)</span> 
<div id="S11.I1.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S11.I1.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S11.I1.i6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Detection is not a task artifact.</span> Removing all task-correlated features (typing speed, scroll speed, keyboard/scroll presence flags, and agent-specific gap features) leaves agent F1 at 1.000 and evasion detection at 100% across all levels (§<a href="#S8" title="8. Task-Domain Ablation ‣ What Does It Take to Detect an AI Agent? Minimal Feature Sets for Behavioral Detection under Browser Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>). The signal is in mouse dynamics and event-class presence, not task identity.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S12" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">12. </span>Discussion &amp; Conclusion</h2>

<section id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">What We Are Actually Detecting.</h4>

<div id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our results show that the primary detection signal arises not from high-level agent reasoning behavior but from low-level execution artifacts introduced by browser automation APIs. In this sense, our detector is better understood as identifying <em id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">automation pipelines</em> than as identifying agent cognition. The “pause-think-act” hypothesis (§<a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1. Agent-Specific Feature Hypotheses ‣ 4. Feature Engineering ‣ What Does It Take to Detect an AI Agent? Minimal Feature Sets for Behavioral Detection under Browser Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>) motivated our agent-specific features, yet none of them appear in the 2-feature backward-elimination necessary set, and all four are removable by step 10 of backward elimination without any drop in agent recall. The signal lives in how automation APIs generate (and fail to generate) events: near-zero raw-mousemove rate, near-zero click-duration variance, absent wheel events. This distinction matters: agents that bypass browser APIs entirely (e.g. via OS-level input simulation or hardware mouse emulators) would likely evade our detector. Extending detection to such paradigms is an important direction for future work.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Why So Few Features Suffice.</h4>

<div id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The backward-elimination necessary features, <span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">mouse_event_rate</span> and <span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">click_duration_std</span>, capture two complementary properties of the <em id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">event stream</em> generated by browser automation APIs: the overall cadence of raw mousemove emissions (essentially zero-or-sparse for Playwright) and the variability of click hold times (essentially zero because programmatic clicks have flat mouseup-after-mousedown delays). Playwright’s <span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">page.mouse.move()</span> and <span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">page.click()</span> generate events at programmatic intervals determined by the execution loop, not by the physical dynamics of a human hand. Even when trajectory coordinates are human-derived (Level 5), the event generation pattern (rate, click-duration variance, presence of event classes) bears the signature of API-driven execution. This is a structural rather than incidental signal, which is why two behavioral features suffice to isolate agents at agent-precision = 1.000 and why the signal is redundantly encoded across <span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">mouse_event_rate</span>, <span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">click_duration_std</span>, <span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">teleport_click_ratio</span>, and the missingness-indicator channels.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Implications for Practitioners.</h4>

<div id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Within the current dominant deployment setting of API-driven browser agents, our results provide a concrete deployment recommendation: instrument {<span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">mouse_event_rate</span>, <span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">click_duration_std</span>} (or the equivalent {<span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">mouse_event_rate</span>, <span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">teleport_click_ratio</span>}) for robust agent isolation, and add <span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">typing_speed_std</span>, <span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">mouse_teleportation</span>, and <span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">scroll_speed_variance</span> for full 3-class discrimination (macro-F1 <math id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\geq" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>≥</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq</annotation></semantics></math> 0.99). The remaining 12 features add instrumentation cost without improving detection. Explicitly, <span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">avoid single-feature deployments</span>: the one solo-“perfect” feature (<span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">cursor_path_linearity</span>) we surfaced collapses to an always-agent classifier and is useless in production. This minimal set is robust against all evasion strategies operating at the trajectory and timing level.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Implications for Evasion.</h4>

<div id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The finding that two features suffice for unit-precision isolation is paradoxically good news for evasion research: it identifies exactly what must be matched. However, the necessary features are event-stream properties (raw mousemove rate, click-duration variance, wheel-event presence) that cannot be controlled through trajectory manipulation or timing sampling; they arise from the CDP-mediated execution of automation APIs themselves. Because Puppeteer, Playwright, and Selenium-with-CDP share the same underlying protocol <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>, <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>)</cite>, we expect the signal to be a structural property of CDP-driven automation rather than a Playwright-specific artifact. Breaking detection would plausibly require abandoning CDP entirely: OS-level input simulation, hardware mouse emulators, DOM-native extension control <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>)</cite>, or pixel-level computer-use agents that feed input through the operating system rather than the DevTools Protocol.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Limitations.</h4>

<div id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our experiments are run on Playwright-driven agents, but the underlying signal is a property of the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) control channel rather than Playwright specifically. Industry analyses report that Puppeteer and Playwright are built on CDP and that agent frameworks “already speak CDP natively” <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>)</cite>, and that CDP-based detection “targets the underlying technology” used by modern automation stacks <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>)</cite>. We therefore expect the teleport-click and event-stream signatures we exploit to generalize to Puppeteer, Selenium 4 with CDP bindings, <span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">chrome.debugger</span>-based extensions, and raw CDP clients that dispatch input via <span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Input.dispatchMouseEvent</span>. However, we are aware of no published cross-framework measurement study that verifies mouse-event timing distributions are empirically equivalent across these stacks, so this generalization remains a testable prediction rather than a demonstrated result. Execution paths that bypass CDP entirely are outside our scope and would likely require different detection approaches: OS-level input injection (e.g., <span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">xdotool</span>, PyAutoGUI, or the macOS Accessibility API used by Anthropic Computer Use <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>)</cite>) traverses the full browser input pipeline and does not exhibit CDP-side effects, and DOM-native extension-based architectures such as rtrvr.ai <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>)</cite> deliberately avoid CDP to evade this class of detector. WebDriver BiDi / Selenium 4’s bidirectional protocol should be treated as uncertain: it is documented as a separate protocol distinct from CDP <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>)</cite>, and whether its timing artifacts converge to the CDP detection surface is an open empirical question. Testing these evasion paths (Puppeteer replication, raw CDP, OS-level injection) is the priority for follow-up work. The exhaustive feature search covers <math id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> = 1…5; the full search space for <math id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> = 6…16 (52,768 additional subsets) would likely show continued growth in perfect-subset density.</p>
</div>
<div id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Claim separation.</em> Our results contain two categories of claims with different evidential strength. <span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Bot-independent claims</span> (the 39.1%/34.5% binary detection gap, 100% three-class agent detection across the full evasion ladder, and the finding that few features suffice for 100% agent recall) rest on real data for both the human and agent sides of the boundary and are unaffected by bot simulation choices. <span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Bot-dependent claims</span> (macro-F1 values and the minimal feature set for 3-class discrimination) depend on our synthetic bot class (three archetypes sampled from literature-grounded Gaussian distributions). While the agent detection results are robust, the specific macro-F1 confidence intervals (<math id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0.986,0.998]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0.986</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.998</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0.986,0.998]</annotation></semantics></math> across SAINT/GBM/RF) and the exact minimal feature set reflect our simulator assumptions and may shift under different bot distributions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Our feature subset optimization uses GradientBoosting rather than SAINT for computational tractability in the exhaustive search (9,401 GBMs over <math id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\binom{17}{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac linethickness="0pt"><mn>17</mn><mi>k</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\binom{17}{k}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> = 1…5); we re-trained SAINT on the <math id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> = 2 best exhaustive subset, the 2-feature backward-elimination necessary set, and the <math id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> = 5 best subset (Table <a href="#S9.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ SAINT validation on minimal subsets. ‣ 9.2. Backward Elimination ‣ 9. Feature Subset Optimization ‣ What Does It Take to Detect an AI Agent? Minimal Feature Sets for Behavioral Detection under Browser Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>). SAINT preserves agent recall = 1.000 at every evasion level on all three subsets; macro-F1 trails the GBM by 0.01–0.03 on the smallest subsets, an expected gap given SAINT’s higher parameter count and our lighter validation training budget (30 epochs with patience 5, vs. the 50-epoch main protocol in Table <a href="#A3.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ Early Stopping. ‣ C.7. Training Procedure ‣ Appendix C SAINT Architecture and Training Details ‣ What Does It Take to Detect an AI Agent? Minimal Feature Sets for Behavioral Detection under Browser Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>). Our agent data covers 10 web tasks driven by a single LLM (Claude) through Playwright and MCP; other LLMs, automation frameworks (Selenium, Puppeteer), and task distributions may produce different behavioral profiles. Human data is sourced from CAPTCHA-solving sessions, which differ in task structure from agent web tasks; our task-domain ablation (§<a href="#S8" title="8. Task-Domain Ablation ‣ What Does It Take to Detect an AI Agent? Minimal Feature Sets for Behavioral Detection under Browser Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>) shows this does not affect agent detection, though future work should validate on matched-task human data. The replay evaluation set is now <math id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> = 524 sessions (all sessions with non-empty event streams in <span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">data/raw/replay_evasion_sessions</span>; the previous count of 165 reflected an earlier snapshot of the same directory, and both replay and feature-optimization scripts now share one loader so counts cannot drift again).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Ethical Considerations.</h4>

<div id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All human behavioral data is sourced from CaptchaSolve30k <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>)</cite>, a publicly available dataset. Our detection research focuses on fundamental API-level signals rather than novel evasion techniques; the evasion methods we evaluate (GAN trajectories, human replay) are well-established in the adversarial ML literature <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>, <a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>)</cite>. While detection techniques could theoretically inform evasion, our findings suggest that the fundamental signal (API-driven event generation) cannot be circumvented without abandoning browser automation APIs entirely, limiting the dual-use risk.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px7" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Reproducibility.</h4>

<div id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All experiments use 70/15/15 stratified train/val/test splits. Key results are validated across 10 random seeds (<math id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> = 42…51) with 95% confidence intervals reported via the <math id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>-distribution (§<a href="#S10" title="10. Multi-Seed Evaluation ‣ What Does It Take to Detect an AI Agent? Minimal Feature Sets for Behavioral Detection under Browser Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>). The complete codebase, trained models, and dataset will be made available upon publication.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px8" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Conclusion.</h4>

<div id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We present the first feature-level analysis of what makes behavioral agent detection work within Playwright-mediated browser automation. Through exhaustive search over 9,401 feature subsets, forward selection, and backward elimination, we show that <span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">two</span> behavioral features suffice for 100% agent recall with unit agent precision at every evasion level: either {<span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px8.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">mouse_event_rate</span>, <span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px8.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">teleport_click_ratio</span>} from the exhaustive search (held-out macro-F1 = 0.926) or {<span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px8.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">mouse_event_rate</span>, <span id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px8.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:90%;">click_duration_std</span>} from backward elimination (macro-F1 = 0.904). Five features are enough to reach macro-F1 <math id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\geq" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>≥</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq</annotation></semantics></math> 0.99 for full three-class discrimination. The <math id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> = 1 regime is degenerate and should not be reported as a deployable result: the one solo-“perfect” indicator we surfaced collapses the classifier to always predict “agent” (agent precision = 0.33, ROC-AUC = 0.5). On the full 17-feature set, 10-seed macro-F1 95% CIs are <math id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px8.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0.986,0.994]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0.986</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.994</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0.986,0.994]</annotation></semantics></math> (SAINT), <math id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px8.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0.993,0.997]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0.993</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.997</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0.993,0.997]</annotation></semantics></math> (RF), and <math id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px8.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0.993,0.998]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0.993</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.998</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0.993,0.998]</annotation></semantics></math> (GBM). The 12–15 features outside the minimal sets are redundant <em id="S12.SS0.SSS0.Px8.p1.1.6" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">within our experimental scope</em> and may prove necessary as agents diversify across frameworks, LLMs, and evasion strategies. A task-domain ablation confirms that the signal resides in event-stream structure, not in task-structural differences between data sources. Detection succeeds because automation APIs do not emit the raw pointer-move and wheel-delta streams that a physical input device produces; the resulting absence signature survives trajectory manipulation. Because Playwright, Puppeteer, and Selenium-with-CDP share the Chrome DevTools Protocol as a common substrate <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>, <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>)</cite>, we expect the signal to generalize across CDP-mediated automation, though empirical verification on non-Playwright stacks is left to future work. The signal is robust, minimal, and actionable within our threat model, and degrades gracefully when any single feature is removed.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Dataset Processing Details</h2>

<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Event Parsing.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The raw data uses two schema formats: (1) <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">tickInputs</span> arrays containing {<math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>, <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">isDown</span>, <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">sampleIndex</span>} objects, and (2) flat arrays of <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>/<math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>/timestamp/button_state values. We implement a unified parser that handles both formats and converts tick indices to millisecond timestamps via <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{\text{ms}}=i\cdot\frac{d}{n_{\text{ticks}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mtext>ms</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mfrac><mi>d</mi><msub><mi>n</mi><mtext>ticks</mtext></msub></mfrac></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{\text{ms}}=i\cdot\frac{d}{n_{\text{ticks}}}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> is the session duration and <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{\text{ticks}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>n</mi><mtext>ticks</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{\text{ticks}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the total tick count (default 4.17 ms/tick for 240 Hz sampling).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Button State Machine.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Rather than treating raw button states as instantaneous signals, we implement a state machine that tracks the previous button state and emits <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">mousedown</span>/<span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">mouseup</span> transitions. This correctly captures click edges (the onset and release of a mouse button press), which are critical for computing click duration features.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Trajectory Segmentation.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We extract cursor movement segments bounded by action events (click, keydown, submit), requiring a minimum of 5 raw points per segment. Each segment is represented in cumulative offset coordinates: <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{p}_{i}=(x_{i}-x_{0},y_{i}-y_{0},t_{i}-t_{0})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐩</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{p}_{i}=(x_{i}-x_{0},y_{i}-y_{0},t_{i}-t_{0})</annotation></semantics></math>, which normalizes for absolute screen position and enables comparison across sessions.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Resampling.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All trajectories are resampled to 60 Hz (<math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta t=16.67" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>16.67</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta t=16.67</annotation></semantics></math> ms) via linear interpolation and normalized to 25 timesteps using <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">numpy.interp</span>. This produces fixed-length trajectory representations suitable for both feature extraction and GAN training.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Feature Definitions</h2>

<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1. </span>Trajectory Features</h3>

<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Trajectory Entropy.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We quantize cursor direction angles into <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> = 20 equal-width bins and compute Shannon entropy:</p>
<table id="A2.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(1)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="H_{\text{traj}}=-\sum_{k=1}^{K}p_{k}\log_{2}p_{k}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mtext>traj</mtext></msub><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.055em">−</mo><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mi>K</mi></msup><mi>p</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>k</mi></msub><mi>log</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\text{traj}}=-\sum_{k=1}^{K}p_{k}\log_{2}p_{k}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> is the fraction of direction changes falling in bin <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>. Higher entropy indicates more varied movement directions, characteristic of human cursor behavior <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Movement Efficiency.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The ratio of straight-line displacement to total path length:</p>
<table id="A2.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(2)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta=\frac{\|\mathbf{p}_{N}-\mathbf{p}_{0}\|}{\sum_{i=1}^{N}\|\mathbf{p}_{i}-\mathbf{p}_{i-1}\|}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐩</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐩</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐩</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐩</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta=\frac{\|\mathbf{p}_{N}-\mathbf{p}_{0}\|}{\sum_{i=1}^{N}\|\mathbf{p}_{i}-\mathbf{p}_{i-1}\|}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Values near 1.0 indicate direct paths (typical of automated movement); lower values indicate the indirect, corrective paths characteristic of human motor control <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">45</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Mouse Teleportation.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The count of instantaneous cursor jumps exceeding a threshold:</p>
<table id="A2.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(3)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=\bigl|\{i:\|\mathbf{p}_{i}-\mathbf{p}_{i-1}\|&gt;\delta_{\text{tp}}\}\bigr|,\quad\delta_{\text{tp}}=100\text{\,px}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐩</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐩</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mtext>tp</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mtext>tp</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext> px</mtext></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=\bigl|\{i:\|\mathbf{p}_{i}-\mathbf{p}_{i-1}\|&gt;\delta_{\text{tp}}\}\bigr|,\quad\delta_{\text{tp}}=100\text{\,px}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Teleportation occurs when browser automation APIs set cursor position directly rather than generating intermediate movement events.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Cursor Path Linearity.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Average linearity over sliding windows of <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>w</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w</annotation></semantics></math> = 10 points:</p>
<table id="A2.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(4)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{W}|}\sum_{(a,b)\in\mathcal{W}}\frac{\|\mathbf{p}_{b}-\mathbf{p}_{a}\|}{\sum_{i=a+1}^{b}\|\mathbf{p}_{i}-\mathbf{p}_{i-1}\|}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐩</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐩</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mi>b</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐩</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐩</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{W}|}\sum_{(a,b)\in\mathcal{W}}\frac{\|\mathbf{p}_{b}-\mathbf{p}_{a}\|}{\sum_{i=a+1}^{b}\|\mathbf{p}_{i}-\mathbf{p}_{i-1}\|}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
