</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{W}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒲</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{W}</annotation></semantics></math> is the set of all consecutive <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>w</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w</annotation></semantics></math>-point windows.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2. </span>Click Features</h3>

<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Click Duration Mean and Std.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Statistics of the time between matched <span id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">mousedown</span> and <span id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">mouseup</span> events:</p>
<table id="A2.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(5)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{d}_{\text{click}}=\frac{1}{n_{c}}\sum_{j=1}^{n_{c}}(t^{\text{up}}_{j}-t^{\text{down}}_{j}),\quad\sigma_{\text{click}}=\text{std}(\{t^{\text{up}}_{j}-t^{\text{down}}_{j}\}_{j=1}^{n_{c}})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mtext>click</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></munderover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>t</mi><mi>j</mi><mtext>up</mtext></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>t</mi><mi>j</mi><mtext>down</mtext></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mtext>click</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>std</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>t</mi><mi>j</mi><mtext>up</mtext></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>t</mi><mi>j</mi><mtext>down</mtext></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{d}_{\text{click}}=\frac{1}{n_{c}}\sum_{j=1}^{n_{c}}(t^{\text{up}}_{j}-t^{\text{down}}_{j}),\quad\sigma_{\text{click}}=\text{std}(\{t^{\text{up}}_{j}-t^{\text{down}}_{j}\}_{j=1}^{n_{c}})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Automation APIs produce unnaturally fast (<math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&lt;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>&lt;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&lt;</annotation></semantics></math>10 ms) and uniform click durations, while human clicks show wider variance (<math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\approx 30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\approx 30</annotation></semantics></math> ms) centered around 100–120 ms <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3. </span>Timing Features</h3>

<section id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Mouse Event Rate.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The frequency of <span id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">mousemove</span> events: <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=|\text{mousemove}|/T_{\text{session}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mtext>mousemove</mtext><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext>session</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=|\text{mousemove}|/T_{\text{session}}</annotation></semantics></math>, measured in Hz. Human interaction produces dense event streams (10–50 Hz), while automation APIs generate sparse, programmatic events <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">47</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Inter-Event Entropy.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Shannon entropy of the distribution of inter-event time gaps across all event types:</p>
<table id="A2.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(6)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E6.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="H_{\text{evt}}=-\sum_{k=1}^{K}p_{k}\log_{2}p_{k}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mtext>evt</mtext></msub><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.055em">−</mo><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mi>K</mi></msup><mi>p</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>k</mi></msub><mi>log</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>p</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\text{evt}}=-\sum_{k=1}^{K}p_{k}\log_{2}p_{k}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">computed over <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> = 20 bins of inter-event gaps. Higher entropy indicates more varied timing, characteristic of human interaction.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Inter-Action Gap Variance and Bimodality.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The variance of gaps between action events (click, keydown, submit) captures timing regularity. Bimodality is measured as the fraction of gaps exceeding a burst threshold:</p>
<table id="A2.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(7)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta=\frac{|\{\Delta t_{i}&gt;\delta_{\text{burst}}\}|}{|\{\Delta t_{i}\}|},\quad\delta_{\text{burst}}=1000\text{\,ms}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>t</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>δ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mtext>burst</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mtext>burst</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1000</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext> ms</mtext></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta=\frac{|\{\Delta t_{i}&gt;\delta_{\text{burst}}\}|}{|\{\Delta t_{i}\}|},\quad\delta_{\text{burst}}=1000\text{\,ms}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Action Burst Ratio.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The complement of bimodality: the fraction of inter-action gaps below the burst threshold:</p>
<table id="A2.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(8)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\text{burst}}=\frac{|\{\Delta t_{i}&lt;\delta_{\text{burst}}\}|}{|\{\Delta t_{i}\}|}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mtext>burst</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>t</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>δ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mtext>burst</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\text{burst}}=\frac{|\{\Delta t_{i}&lt;\delta_{\text{burst}}\}|}{|\{\Delta t_{i}\}|}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Agents exhibit high burst ratios due to rapid-fire actions during the “act” phase of their pause-think-act cycle.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Time to First Action.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The delay <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{\text{first\_action}}-t_{\text{first\_event}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mtext>first_action</mtext></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mtext>first_event</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{\text{first\_action}}-t_{\text{first\_event}}</annotation></semantics></math> captures the “page read time” before the first interaction.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Typing Speed Mean and Std.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Statistics of inter-keydown intervals. Human typing shows high variance (<math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\approx 55" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>55</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\approx 55</annotation></semantics></math> ms) reflecting natural motor variability, while automation produces uniform timing.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.4. </span>Agent-Specific Features</h3>

<section id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Teleport-Click Ratio.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The fraction of clicks preceded by cursor teleportation:</p>
<table id="A2.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(9)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\text{tc}}=\min\!\left(1,\frac{\tau}{n_{\text{clicks}}}\right)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mtext>tc</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.653em;" width="1.653em"><mi>min</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>τ</mi><msub><mi>n</mi><mtext>clicks</mtext></msub></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\text{tc}}=\min\!\left(1,\frac{\tau}{n_{\text{clicks}}}\right)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">This is the single most discriminative feature in our analysis (§<a href="#S9" title="9. Feature Subset Optimization ‣ What Does It Take to Detect an AI Agent? Minimal Feature Sets for Behavioral Detection under Browser Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>), as automation APIs typically move the cursor to the target element and immediately click, producing a characteristic teleport-then-click pattern.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Scroll Speed Variance.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The variance of inter-scroll-event time gaps: <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{Var}(\{\Delta t_{\text{scroll}}\})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>Var</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mtext>scroll</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{Var}(\{\Delta t_{\text{scroll}}\})</annotation></semantics></math>. Programmatic scrolling produces uniform intervals, while human scrolling is irregular.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.5. </span>Feature Normalization</h3>

<div id="A2.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All continuous features are min-max normalized to <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A2.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(10)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{x}_{i}=\frac{x_{i}-x_{\min}}{x_{\max}-x_{\min}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>min</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>min</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{x}_{i}=\frac{x_{i}-x_{\min}}{x_{\max}-x_{\min}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS5.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{\min}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{\min}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{\max}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{\max}</annotation></semantics></math> fitted on the balanced training set only. For nullable features, we add binary indicator columns <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="h_{i}=\mathbb{1}[x_{i}\neq\text{null}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>𝟙</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>≠</mo><mtext>null</mtext><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{i}=\mathbb{1}[x_{i}\neq\text{null}]</annotation></semantics></math>. Binary features are directly converted to <span id="A2.SS5.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">float32</span>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>SAINT Architecture and Training Details</h2>

<section id="A3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.1. </span>Per-Feature Embedding</h3>

<div id="A3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Unlike vision or language tasks where inputs share a common modality, tabular features are heterogeneous: each feature has its own scale, distribution, and semantics. Following SAINT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>)</cite> and FT-Transformer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>)</cite>, we project each feature independently into a shared embedding space.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For each continuous feature <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A3.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in\mathcal{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in\mathcal{C}</annotation></semantics></math>), we learn a separate linear projection:</p>
<table id="A3.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(11)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{e}_{i}=\mathbf{W}_{i}x_{i}+\mathbf{b}_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝐛</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{e}_{i}=\mathbf{W}_{i}x_{i}+\mathbf{b}_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times 1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times 1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{b}_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐛</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{b}_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>. For each binary feature <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A3.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j\in\mathcal{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j\in\mathcal{B}</annotation></semantics></math>), we use a learned embedding lookup:</p>
<table id="A3.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(12)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{e}_{j}=\texttt{Embed}_{j}(b_{j})\in\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">Embed</mtext><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{e}_{j}=\texttt{Embed}_{j}(b_{j})\in\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS1.p2.3" class="ltx_p">where <span id="A3.SS1.p2.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Embed<sub id="A3.SS1.p2.3.1.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="A3.SS1.p2.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">j</span></sub></span> is a <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\times d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\times d</annotation></semantics></math> embedding table. This per-feature approach allows each feature to learn its own representation, in contrast to TabTransformer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>)</cite> which only applies attention to categorical features. We use <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> = 32 throughout.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.2. </span>CLS Token and Positional Encoding</h3>

<div id="A3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A learnable CLS token <math id="A3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{c}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐜</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{c}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> is prepended to the feature embedding sequence, following the BERT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">32</a>)</cite> convention for aggregating sequence-level representations. Learnable positional encodings <math id="A3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{P}\in\mathbb{R}^{(n+1)\times d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐏</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{P}\in\mathbb{R}^{(n+1)\times d}</annotation></semantics></math> are added:</p>
<table id="A3.E13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(13)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{S}^{(0)}=[\mathbf{c};\,\mathbf{e}_{1};\,\ldots;\,\mathbf{e}_{n}]+\mathbf{P}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐒</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>𝐜</mi><mo rspace="0.337em">;</mo><msub><mi>𝐞</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo rspace="0.337em">;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo rspace="0.337em">;</mo><msub><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>𝐏</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{S}^{(0)}=[\mathbf{c};\,\mathbf{e}_{1};\,\ldots;\,\mathbf{e}_{n}]+\mathbf{P}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">We use learnable rather than sinusoidal positional encodings because tabular features have no inherent sequential ordering; the positional encoding must learn which features interact most strongly, rather than encoding proximity.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.3. </span>Transformer Blocks</h3>

<div id="A3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The embedded sequence passes through <math id="A3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> = 2 transformer blocks. Each block applies multi-head self-attention <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">31</a>)</cite> followed by a position-wise feed-forward network (FFN), with residual connections and layer normalization:</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Multi-Head Self-Attention.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">With <math id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> = 4 attention heads:</p>
<table id="A3.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.E14"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(14)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.E14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\text{Attn}(\mathbf{Q},\mathbf{K},\mathbf{V})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>Attn</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐐</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐊</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐕</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\text{Attn}(\mathbf{Q},\mathbf{K},\mathbf{V})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.E14.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\text{softmax}\!\left(\frac{\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^{\top}}{\sqrt{d_{k}}}\right)\mathbf{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:3.720em;" width="3.720em"><mtext>softmax</mtext></mpadded><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msup><mi>𝐐𝐊</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><msqrt><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msqrt></mfrac></mstyle><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐕</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\text{softmax}\!\left(\frac{\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^{\top}}{\sqrt{d_{k}}}\right)\mathbf{V}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A3.E15"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(15)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.E15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\text{head}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mtext>head</mtext><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\text{head}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.E15.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\text{Attn}(\mathbf{S}\mathbf{W}_{i}^{Q},\mathbf{S}\mathbf{W}_{i}^{K},\mathbf{S}\mathbf{W}_{i}^{V})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>Attn</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐒𝐖</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>Q</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐒𝐖</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>K</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐒𝐖</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>V</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\text{Attn}(\mathbf{S}\mathbf{W}_{i}^{Q},\mathbf{S}\mathbf{W}_{i}^{K},\mathbf{S}\mathbf{W}_{i}^{V})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A3.E16"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(16)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.E16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\text{MHA}(\mathbf{S})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>MHA</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐒</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\text{MHA}(\mathbf{S})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.E16.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=[\text{head}_{1};\ldots;\text{head}_{h}]\mathbf{W}^{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mtext>head</mtext><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>;</mo><msub><mtext>head</mtext><mi>h</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>O</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=[\text{head}_{1};\ldots;\text{head}_{h}]\mathbf{W}^{O}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{k}=d/h=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{k}=d/h=8</annotation></semantics></math>. Self-attention allows each feature to attend to every other feature, learning cross-feature interactions that are critical for tabular data <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Feed-Forward Network.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A two-layer FFN with GELU activation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>)</cite> and expansion factor 2:</p>
<table id="A3.E17" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

</div>
</section>

</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Why 2 Blocks Suffice.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Unlike NLP or vision tasks where deep stacks capture hierarchical abstractions over long sequences, tabular data has a fixed, small number of features (<math id="A3.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> = 16–23). Two attention layers allow each feature to attend to all others directly (layer 1) and to attend to those attention-informed representations (layer 2), which suffices for capturing pairwise and higher-order feature interactions. Empirically, adding more blocks yielded no improvement on our dataset.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.4. </span>Denoising Pre-Training</h3>

<div id="A3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Following SAINT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>)</cite>, we pre-train the encoder using a denoising objective. For each sample, we randomly mask 30% of input features by replacing them with zeros. The encoder processes the corrupted input, and per-feature reconstruction heads predict the original values from the encoded representations.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For continuous features, a linear head predicts the original value:</p>
<table id="A3.E20" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(20)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{x}_{i}=\mathbf{w}_{i}^{\top}\mathbf{s}_{i}+c_{i}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐰</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{x}_{i}=\mathbf{w}_{i}^{\top}\mathbf{s}_{i}+c_{i}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS4.p2.2" class="ltx_p">For binary features, a linear head followed by sigmoid predicts the original label:</p>
<table id="A3.E21" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(21)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E21.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{b}_{j}=\sigma(\mathbf{w}_{j}^{\top}\mathbf{s}_{j}+c_{j})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>b</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐰</mi><mi>j</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{b}_{j}=\sigma(\mathbf{w}_{j}^{\top}\mathbf{s}_{j}+c_{j})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS4.p2.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{s}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{s}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is the encoder’s output for the <math id="A3.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>-th feature token (CLS token excluded).</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The denoising loss is computed only over masked positions:</p>
<table id="A3.E22" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(22)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E22.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{denoise}}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{M}_{c}|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{M}_{c}}(x_{i}-\hat{x}_{i})^{2}+\frac{1}{|\mathcal{M}_{b}|}\sum_{j\in\mathcal{M}_{b}}\text{BCE}(b_{j},\hat{b}_{j})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>denoise</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow></munder><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow></munder><mrow><mtext>BCE</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>b</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{denoise}}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{M}_{c}|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{M}_{c}}(x_{i}-\hat{x}_{i})^{2}+\frac{1}{|\mathcal{M}_{b}|}\sum_{j\in\mathcal{M}_{b}}\text{BCE}(b_{j},\hat{b}_{j})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS4.p3.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{c}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{b}</annotation></semantics></math> are the sets of masked continuous and binary features, respectively. Pre-training uses a separate Adam optimizer and runs for 50 epochs before supervised fine-tuning begins.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS4.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS4.p4.1" class="ltx_p">We choose denoising over contrastive pre-training because our dataset is small (<math id="A3.SS4.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>6,000 samples): contrastive methods require diverse positive pairs to learn useful representations, while denoising directly learns feature dependencies from individual samples. This aligns with findings that denoising pre-training is more effective than contrastive objectives for small tabular datasets <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.5. </span>Binary Classification Head</h3>

<div id="A3.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For the binary (human-vs-bot) detection task, the CLS token output feeds a two-layer classification head:</p>
<table id="A3.E23" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(23)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E23.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{y}=\sigma(\mathbf{w}_{2}^{\top}\text{ReLU}(\mathbf{W}_{1}\mathbf{s}_{\text{CLS}}+\mathbf{b}_{1})+b_{2})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐰</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>ReLU</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐬</mi><mtext>CLS</mtext></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝐛</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y}=\sigma(\mathbf{w}_{2}^{\top}\text{ReLU}(\mathbf{W}_{1}\mathbf{s}_{\text{CLS}}+\mathbf{b}_{1})+b_{2})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS5.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{1}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{1}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}</annotation></semantics></math>. Training uses binary cross-entropy with logits (BCEWithLogitsLoss). We use CLS token pooling rather than mean pooling over all feature tokens because the CLS token learns to aggregate information during attention, acting as a global summary <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">32</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.6. </span>Three-Class Adaptation</h3>

<div id="A3.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For three-class detection (human/bot/agent), we replace the binary head with a multi-class head:</p>
<table id="A3.E24" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(24)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E24.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mathbf{y}}=\mathbf{W}_{2}\cdot\text{Dropout}(\text{ReLU}(\mathbf{W}_{1}\mathbf{s}_{\text{CLS}}+\mathbf{b}_{1}))+\mathbf{b}_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{3}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐲</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mtext>Dropout</mtext></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext>ReLU</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐬</mi><mtext>CLS</mtext></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝐛</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝐛</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mathbf{y}}=\mathbf{W}_{2}\cdot\text{Dropout}(\text{ReLU}(\mathbf{W}_{1}\mathbf{s}_{\text{CLS}}+\mathbf{b}_{1}))+\mathbf{b}_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{3}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS6.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with Dropout(<math id="A3.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> = 0.1) for regularization. Training uses cross-entropy loss with optional class weighting to handle any residual class imbalance after downsampling.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The key insight is that the <em id="A3.SS6.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">same encoder architecture</em> supports both tasks: only the classification head changes. Yet the three-class model achieves dramatically different detection capability: perfect agent detection (F1 = 1.000) where the binary SAINT model allows 34.5% evasion (MLP 39.1%).</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS6.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Expected Calibration Error.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate prediction calibration using ECE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">35</a>)</cite> with <math id="A3.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> = 10 confidence bins:</p>
<table id="A3.E25" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(25)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E25.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{ECE}=\sum_{m=1}^{M}\frac{|B_{m}|}{n}|\text{acc}(B_{m})-\text{conf}(B_{m})|" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>ECE</mtext><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>M</mi></munderover><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><mtext>acc</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mtext>conf</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{ECE}=\sum_{m=1}^{M}\frac{|B_{m}|}{n}|\text{acc}(B_{m})-\text{conf}(B_{m})|</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{m}</annotation></semantics></math> is the set of samples whose maximum predicted probability falls in bin <math id="A3.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{acc}(B_{m})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>acc</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{acc}(B_{m})</annotation></semantics></math> is the accuracy within that bin, and <math id="A3.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{conf}(B_{m})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>conf</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{conf}(B_{m})</annotation></semantics></math> is the mean predicted confidence.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS7" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.7. </span>Training Procedure</h3>

<div id="A3.SS7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Supervised fine-tuning follows the denoising pre-training phase described in §<a href="#A3.SS4" title="C.4. Denoising Pre-Training ‣ Appendix C SAINT Architecture and Training Details ‣ What Does It Take to Detect an AI Agent? Minimal Feature Sets for Behavioral Detection under Browser Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.4</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS7.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Optimizer.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Adam <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>)</cite> with learning rate <math id="A3.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta=10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta=10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math> and weight decay <math id="A3.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda=10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda=10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS7.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Learning Rate Schedule.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Cosine annealing <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>)</cite>:</p>
<table id="A3.E26" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(26)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E26.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta_{t}=\eta_{\min}+\frac{1}{2}(\eta_{\max}-\eta_{\min})\left(1+\cos\frac{t\pi}{T}\right)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>min</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><mi>T</mi></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta_{t}=\eta_{\min}+\frac{1}{2}(\eta_{\max}-\eta_{\min})\left(1+\cos\frac{t\pi}{T}\right)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> is the total number of epochs.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS7.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Early Stopping.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We monitor validation macro-F1 with patience of 15 epochs. The best model checkpoint (highest validation macro-F1) is restored after training completes.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS7.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A3.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ Early Stopping. ‣ C.7. <td id="A3.T9.5.12.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="A3.T9.5.12.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Cosine annealing</span></td></tr>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A3.F7.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 7</span>. </span><span id="A3.F7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">SAINT architecture for behavioral agent detection. Input features are independently embedded (continuous via linear projection, binary via embedding lookup), combined with a learnable CLS token and positional encoding, and processed by two transformer blocks. The CLS output feeds either a binary or three-class classification head. During pre-training, feature tokens feed a denoising reconstruction head (dashed).</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Evasion Methodology</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We construct a five-level evasion ladder of escalating attacker sophistication. Level 1 (no evasion) uses unmodified agent behavior. Levels 2–5 apply progressively stronger evasion techniques to test whether detection relies on superficial or fundamental signals.</p>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1. </span>Rule-Based Evasion (Level 2)</h3>

<div id="A4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Rule-based evasion applies hand-crafted humanization to the agent’s browser interactions. We implement three sub-levels of increasing sophistication:</p>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Mild.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Random inter-action delays sampled from <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U(500,2000)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>500</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2000</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U(500,2000)</annotation></semantics></math> ms. Sequential key presses with random per-character delays in <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[80,200]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>80,200</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[80,200]</annotation></semantics></math> ms. No cursor movement simulation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Moderate.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In addition to timing delays, we simulate human-like cursor movement before each click using quadratic Bézier interpolation. Given start point <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{p}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐩</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{p}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> and target <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{p}_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐩</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{p}_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, we compute a control point <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{p}_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐩</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{p}_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> with random offsets (<math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm 50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 50</annotation></semantics></math> px horizontal, <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm 30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 30</annotation></semantics></math> px vertical) and interpolate:</p>
<table id="A4.E27" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(27)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E27.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{B}(t)=(1-t)^{2}\mathbf{p}_{0}+2(1-t)t\,\mathbf{p}_{1}+t^{2}\mathbf{p}_{2},\quad t\in[0,1]" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>𝐁</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐩</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐩</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐩</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{B}(t)=(1-t)^{2}\mathbf{p}_{0}+2(1-t)t\,\mathbf{p}_{1}+t^{2}\mathbf{p}_{2},\quad t\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">sampled at 15 steps with 8–25 ms per step, producing a 40–125 Hz movement rate. Gaussian micro-jitter <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{N}(0,1.5)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{N}(0,1.5)</annotation></semantics></math> px is added per step.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Aggressive.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Additional humanization: pre-task scrolling (<math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm 50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 50</annotation></semantics></math>–150 px), curved cursor paths (20–25 Bézier steps with stronger control point offsets), typing rhythm variation (base delay 130–140 ms, variation factor 0.55–0.6), idle micro-movements (3–8 resting hand gestures with Gaussian drift), and page read simulation between major actions.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.2. </span>Conditional WGAN-GP (Levels 3–4)</h3>

<div id="A4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For GAN-based evasion, we train a conditional Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">48</a>, <a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>)</cite> on 14,342 real human trajectory segments from CaptchaSolve30k <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Generator.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G(\mathbf{z},\mathbf{c})\to\mathbb{R}^{T\times 3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐳</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐜</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G(\mathbf{z},\mathbf{c})\to\mathbb{R}^{T\times 3}</annotation></semantics></math> maps noise <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{z}\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{I}_{64})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐳</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>𝟎</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐈</mi><mn>64</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{z}\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{I}_{64})</annotation></semantics></math> and condition <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{c}=(d,\theta,T_{\text{dur}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐜</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mtext>dur</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{c}=(d,\theta,T_{\text{dur}})</annotation></semantics></math> (distance, angle, duration) to a trajectory of <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> = 25 displacement steps <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta t)</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A4.E28" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(28)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E28.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G:\mathbb{R}^{64}\times\mathbb{R}^{3}\xrightarrow{\text{FC-BN-ReLU}}\mathbb{R}^{512}\xrightarrow{\text{FC-BN-ReLU}}\mathbb{R}^{75}\xrightarrow{\tanh}\mathbb{R}^{25\times 3}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>64</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mtext mathsize="0.700em">FC-BN-ReLU</mtext></mover><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>512</mn></msup><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mtext mathsize="0.700em">FC-BN-ReLU</mtext></mover><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>75</mn></msup><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mo mathsize="0.700em">tanh</mo></mover><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G:\mathbb{R}^{64}\times\mathbb{R}^{3}\xrightarrow{\text{FC-BN-ReLU}}\mathbb{R}^{512}\xrightarrow{\text{FC-BN-ReLU}}\mathbb{R}^{75}\xrightarrow{\tanh}\mathbb{R}^{25\times 3}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Output displacements are scaled by distance (<math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta x,\Delta y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta x,\Delta y</annotation></semantics></math>) and duration (<math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta t</annotation></semantics></math>) from the condition vector.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Discriminator.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{c})\to\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐜</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{c})\to\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math> scores trajectories (higher = more realistic), with no sigmoid, consistent with the Wasserstein formulation:</p>
<table id="A4.E29" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(29)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E29.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D:\mathbb{R}^{78}\xrightarrow{\text{FC-LeakyReLU-Drop}}\mathbb{R}^{512}\xrightarrow{\text{FC-LeakyReLU-Drop}}\mathbb{R}^{256}\xrightarrow{\text{FC}}\mathbb{R}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>78</mn></msup><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mtext mathsize="0.700em">FC-LeakyReLU-Drop</mtext></mover><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>512</mn></msup><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mtext mathsize="0.700em">FC-LeakyReLU-Drop</mtext></mover><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>256</mn></msup><mover accent="true"><mo>→</mo><mtext mathsize="0.700em">FC</mtext></mover><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D:\mathbb{R}^{78}\xrightarrow{\text{FC-LeakyReLU-Drop}}\mathbb{R}^{512}\xrightarrow{\text{FC-LeakyReLU-Drop}}\mathbb{R}^{256}\xrightarrow{\text{FC}}\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with LeakyReLU(<math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> = 0.2) and Dropout(<math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> = 0.3).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Training Objective.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The discriminator minimizes:</p>
<table id="A4.E30" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(30)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E30.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{D}=\underset{\mathbf{z}}{\mathbb{E}}[D(G(\mathbf{z},\mathbf{c}),\mathbf{c})]-\underset{\mathbf{x}}{\mathbb{E}}[D(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{c})]+\lambda_{\text{GP}}\underset{\hat{\mathbf{x}}}{\mathbb{E}}\!\left[(\|\nabla_{\hat{\mathbf{x}}}D(\hat{\mathbf{x}},\mathbf{c})\|_{2}-1)^{2}\right]" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><munder accentunder="true"><mi>𝔼</mi><mo mathsize="0.700em">𝐱</mo></munder><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐜</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>GP</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><munder accentunder="true"><mi>𝔼</mi><mover accent="true"><mi
